name: Can you convert a tub to a shower in a condo or apartment building?

mainEntity.name: Can a bathtub be converted to a shower in a condo, townhouse, or apartment-style unit?
mainEntity.text: Can a bathtub be converted to a shower in a condo, townhouse, or apartment-style unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tub-to-shower conversion in a condo or apartment-style unit is possible, but there are extra rules to check first. Building management or an HOA may require approval, specific work hours, insurance documentation, or approved contractors. Plumbing access can also be more limited than in a detached house, especially if the drain or supply lines run through shared walls or stacked systems. Noise, debris removal, and waterproofing requirements may be stricter too. Homeowners should confirm whether the unit allows fixture changes and whether any building-specific inspections are needed. It is also wise to verify that the contractor has experience working in multi-unit buildings, because coordination matters as much as the install itself. A good plan should protect neighbors below and beside the bathroom and ensure the finished shower meets both building rules and long-term maintenance needs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but it often depends on building rules, noise restrictions, plumbing access, and approval requirements from the HOA or property manager. Shared walls and stacked plumbing can make the project more complex than in a single-family home.
